message.reasoning_content:
t6 shows all 36 cases fail even on benign-looking inputs (negative int32 words everywhere though — my generator used full int32 range, so high nibbles arbitrary... but actually qweight has exactly ceil(K/8) rows, so all nibbles are used within those rows except high nibbles of final row when K%8!=0. For K=1 case: qweight is 1 row, nibbles 1..7 unused → arbitrary allowed. Fail with maxerr 0.21 for K=1. Also "FAIL 63 16 52 16" K=16: all nibbles used, so failure isn't from unused nibbles. But negative words: quant extraction via (value >> shift) & 15 in kernel: value loaded as int32 then .to(tl.uint32) — fine bit-wise. But in Triton, `value >> (4*(original_k%8))` on int32 does arithmetic shift; masking &15 fixes it. Fine.

Hmm, but failure even for K=16 with all nibbles used and monotone? No, g_idx permuted. Errors are massive (0.2–1.7) — looks like a real bug, or my reference differs. My probe used K.reference — the kernel's own reference, which should be correct per contract. But also my probe's qweight rows use random full int32 — that's legal.

But wait — the massive failures across all cases suggests possibly a probe artifact: e.g., repack mask issue with original_k: `original_k = tl.load(ORDER + sorted_k, mask=sorted_k < K, other=0)` — ORDER has K entries; sorted_k ranges up to tile_k*16+15 which can exceed K; masked fine.

Finalize t6 as confirmed, then run one more probe with benign make_inputs (the kernel's own generator, guaranteed valid) plus a tiny controlled case to rule out probe construction issues. That's what t7 attempted. Do that.
